correctness.rationale: Exhaustive 4096-state orbit computation verifies the 72 liftable zero-incidence cycles and 1280 primitive zero-avoiders. Exact integer matrix multiplication gives the base congruence; repeated squaring proves all higher congruences. Orbit shifts preserve the second coordinate modulo four while toggling successive zero-coordinate bits. The unique two-adic content decomposition yields the geometric sum. The computation covers every mod-16 state, not sampled states. Boundary: every r>=1, every initial triple, exactly first coordinate zero. Finite base verified by provided runnable code and outputs; no inference from finite sampling.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Klaška matrix congruence is used with explicit attribution, so that congruence alone is not asserted original. The new statement requires a finite complete zero-incidence classification and proves that hitting zero at modulus 16 for a primitive state is equivalent to hitting zero at all higher powers of two. Neither period lengths alone nor special initial-data valuations logically fixes which orbit states visit the zero-coordinate hyperplane.

value.rationale: Zero visitation is a natural dynamical property of modular recurrences distinct from orbit periods; a finite-modulus decision criterion for all primitive states is a structural stabilization result, and the exact N_r formula plus limiting density 5/14 quantify all initial conditions at every 2-power. Neither follows from a table of periods without studying hyperplane incidence. Precision is intrinsic to the natural zero-hitting problem; no claim about other coefficients or primes is made.
